item.description: When it comes to the balance sheet, as with all of the Fed’s work, the focus needs to be on how we can best serve the public and support a strong economy and financial system.

item.title: Opening remarks for panel titled ‘Economic uncertainty and the design and conduct of monetary policy’
item.description: The relevance of economic uncertainty to monetary policy is both timely and timeless. Timely, because this is a moment of substantial uncertainty about the economic outlook. Timeless, because uncertainty is a pervasive feature of the macroeconomy and monetary policymaking.

item.title: Ample liquidity for a safe and efficient banking system
item.description: Dallas Fed President Lorie discusses the stance of monetary policy and how the Fed's balance sheet fosters a safe and efficient liquidity environment for the U.S. banking system.

item.title: Why I’ll be cautious about further rate cuts
item.description: While the labor market has undeniably slowed, not all of the slowing represents economic slack, and inflation remains persistently above target.

item.title: The case for modernizing the FOMC’s operating target rate
item.description: The time has come for the FOMC to prepare to target a different short-term interest rate. A repo rate would provide a more robust target than the current fed funds target.

item.title: Opening remarks for panel titled ‘Post-Pandemic Challenges for Monetary Policy Implementation’
item.description: At the Banco de México’s conference on the future of central banking, President Lorie Logan discussed how central banks can return their assets and liabilities to normal after expanding their balance sheets in response to the pandemic.

item.title: Opening remarks for moderated conversation at the World Affairs Council of San Antonio
item.description: Dallas Fed President Logan's base case is that monetary policy needs to hold tight for a while longer to bring inflation sustainably back to target, but she believes it's also quite plausible that some combination of softer inflation and a weakening labor market will call for lower rates fairly soon.

item.title: Opening remarks for Fed Listens

item.title: Efficient and effective central bank balance sheets
item.description: At a Bank of England conference on central bank balance sheets, President Lorie Logan laid out two key principles: efficient and effective. It’s heartening that central banks around the world have converged on some approaches to uphold these twin principles.

item.title: Navigating in shallow waters: Monetary policy strategy in a better-balanced economy
item.description: After a voyage through rough waters, the shore is in sight: the FOMC’s Congressionally mandated goals of maximum employment and stable prices. But the ship hasn't tied up yet, and risks remain that could push the economy back out to sea or slam it into the dock too hard.
